findings.where: the six voice-note cards; largest at y 544-702 x 520-917, and the one the build's own check names at (1280,2640)
findings.what: Six card interiors are a single literal RGB value #F1ECDF (241,236,223) with zero variance: 179,258 px in all, 3.99 per cent of the frame, the six regions 24,921 / 27,454 / 27,962 / 30,228 / 31,820 / 36,873 px; four of the six contain exactly one unique colour across their whole area, a 40x40 box at (1280,2640) has one unique colour and luma std 0.0000, row y=1050 runs one colour unbroken across 350 px from x 1010 to 1360, and in a 370x140 block round region 3 39,899 of 51,800 pixels are that one value with the remainder being the waveform and the caption drawn over it.
findings.why: The row ends 'Any procedural noise overlay, tiled repeating texture, or beige rounded rectangle standing in for paper scores this category below its floor'; a beige rectangle with a torn outline drawn round it is that rectangle, and evidence/logs/flat.json reaches the same verdict on its own evidence (ok: false, files_with_a_flat_fill: 1) while naming the identical construct in its negative control, 'a_flat_fill_of_0xFFF3EEE3 ... the literal Container colour that used to stand in for a sheet in authoring.dart', one grey level away from what is still on the glass.

findings.where: the crop named 'shadow', taken at 300 per cent from 02_chat.png at box [579,1885,999,2145]; then every sheet edge in every still
findings.what: There is no contact shadow. On the shadow crop I traced the paper/wood boundary per column and sampled the wood beneath it: 105.09 at 4 crop px, 94.87 at 8, 91.41 at 12, then 90.7 / 89.7 / 89.6 / 89.1 / 89.1 / 90.2 / 88.8 out to 380 crop px (127 native px) - brighter at the line of contact than away from it, which is the inverse of a contact shadow. On the whole of 02_chat.png, binning desk pixels by the outward direction to the nearest sheet and by distance, all eight directions read between 86.1 and 97.5 from 4 px to 100 px against a far-desk mean of 86.6 and a desk texture std of 16.5; up reads 92.8/90.1/89.7/89.5/89.2/87.5 and down 93.8/91.1/89.9/90.2/90.4/91.4, under two grey levels apart at every distance. Run the same band (3-12 px out, scaled for the stills' 1.333x) on all ten: the deepest side is 0.5 below far desk in 02_chat, 0.0 in 13_messenger_states and 17_setup_pwa, 0.5 in 10_first_run, 5.7 in 01_pulse, 6.5 in 03_us, 7.0 in 12_search, and in 04_moments and dusk_pulse every side is brighter than the far desk. Stretching the desk's own 2-98 per cent range over a 1200x400 strip through a sheet edge in 01_pulse, 03_us, 02_chat and dusk_pulse shows no darkening band at any edge in any of the four. The same is true of the feeling objects: round the 'hold' object in 01_pulse.png every side reads brighter than the desk 90 px out (up 88.9, down 129.5, left 90.8, right 90.0 against 77.1), and round it in dusk_pulse.png the deepest side is 1.0 grey level down.
findings.why: The row requires 'contact shadows baked from the render's own lighting rather than applied as a uniform blur', and names the Chat hero at three hundred per cent as where it is judged; the hero has no shadow of either kind, so there is no light direction in it to read. The capability plainly exists - in 06_unfolding.mp4 frame 285 the desk 3-12 px below a sheet reads 69.8 against 91.8 far away while the desk above it reads 90.5, a 22.0-level directional shadow, and in 07_feeling_landing frames 11-91 the object darkens the paper on its left by 6-12 levels - so what the stills show is the shadow being dropped between the clip path and the still path, not a renderer that cannot cast one.

findings.where: every free paper-against-desk edge; the hero's are at crops/02_chat_300_edge.png and 02_chat_300_hand.png
findings.what: The torn edges are very nearly straight. Tracing every boundary run of 300 columns or more and high-passing it over 31 columns, 02_chat.png gives 22 edges with rms 0.20 to 2.71 px, median 0.71, and 13 of the 22 under 1.0 px; the tear in the 300 per cent shadow crop measures rms 2.39 crop px = 0.80 native px over a 420-native-px run. Across the set the per-still medians are 05_settings 0.38, 03_us 0.47, 04_moments 0.54, 01_pulse 0.55, 02_chat 0.71, 12_search 0.72, 14_media_viewer 0.81, 13_messenger_states 0.94, 10_first_run 1.12, 17_setup_pwa 1.30.
findings.why: evidence/logs/torn.json supplies the calibration itself: edges a critic was content with measured rms 2.88 to 5.14 on the glass and the ones they were not 0.36 to 0.59. Nine of the ten stills have a median edge below 1.30 and five are inside the rejected band, so what is on the glass reads as a guillotined edge with a fringe of hair strokes pasted along it rather than as a tear. The same log states the cause and that it was not acted on - 'the fracture's Hurst exponent runs to 1.15, and 1.15 is a clean pull, and a clean pull is too clean... Not re-rendered this cycle' - and its headline pass (max_corr 0.45, worst_self_correlation 0.339, ok: true) is measured on blender/rig/common.torn_edge, the rig's profile generator, not on the 56 masks the app draws, whose rms the same file gives as min 1.15, median 2.0, with 28 of 56 under 2.

findings.where: the arriving note, frames 109, 113 and 117 (app time 1.74 s, 1.81 s, 1.87 s at 16 ms a frame)
findings.what: The unfolding piece is torn along its top and bottom and guillotined down both sides. Over its 313-row silhouette the left edge measures rms 0.46 to 0.57 px after a 31-row trend is removed and the right edge 1.00 to 1.07 px, peak to peak 3 to 8 px.
findings.why: Against torn.json's own bands those two sides sit at or below the level it records as rejected, so the piece reads as a rectangle with two decorated edges rather than as something torn out of a sheet.

findings.where: the hinge line of the fold, frame 113, rows y 1202-1221 averaged across x 40 px inside each edge
findings.what: There is no specular line at the crease. The rows across the hinge read 86, 86, 86, 86, 86, 86, 86, 86, 86, 86, 86, 87, 95, 123, 167, 209, 221, 226, 230, 231 - a monotone ramp from desk to the face's own tone, topping out at 231 where the flat face beside it also reads 230-241.
findings.why: The row asks for 'folds and creases'; the fold itself is genuinely rendered, but a crease in paper catches a highlight brighter than the flat sheet either side of it and this one has none, so the hinge reads as a boundary between two shaded planes rather than as a folded fibre.

findings.what: The check reports flattest 0.554 at (400,720) and windows_under_the_floor 0 against its own derived floor of 0.461, but the same 80x80 window measured at (300,700) reads 0.234, at (60,670) 0.366 and at (100,680) 0.467; the region y 660-788 x 48-807 holds 40x40 blocks with 2 to 6 unique colours. The 80-pixel stride steps over the flattest part of the area it is reporting on.
findings.why: The verdict the log reaches about that file is right and I agree with it - my own probes show a photographed sky carrying sensor grain, content rather than a surface the build answers for - but the number it publishes for its own gate is not the lowest the same check finds, and a floor reported from a stride that misses the minimum cannot be relied on next cycle.

what_is_working: Handwriting has real variants and real pressure, measured independently of the build's own log. Taking ink as luma<130 on paper in 02_chat.png and keeping the 444 components between 60 and 6000 px, normalising each to 48x48 and comparing every pair: median best-match IoU 0.767, p90 0.918, max 0.984, and ZERO components with a twin at IoU 0.99 or above - a font repeated would sit near 1.0 on every repeat. Pressure: over 458 glyphs, the darkness of the stroke core (at least 1.5 px in from the edge, so not the antialias rim) varies within a single glyph by a median std of 11.85 and a median range of 49.84 grey levels, and glyph to glyph by 14.01. Stroke width along the ridge varies within a glyph by a median 1.09 px on a 4.23 px mean stroke and glyph to glyph by 1.32 px, 31 per cent of the mean. This corroborates logs/hand.json (median 0.719, 0.004 at IoU 0.99) on a separate segmentation.

No tiled repeating texture - the second of the row's three automatic-fail conditions, tested with a control. Zero-padded linear autocorrelation of the grain on ink-free patches: 02_chat 0.167 at lag 57, 05_settings 0.318 at 14, 01_pulse 0.214 at 27, 12_search 0.223 at 17, 17_setup_pwa 0.284 at 14, 13_messenger_states 0.303 at 14, 04_moments 0.144 at 88 - all low and none at a repeating period. A synthetic 64-px tile put through the same code reads 0.840 at exactly dx=64. And the grain of two different notes in 02_chat.png correlates 0.072 over all shifts, so no texture patch is reused between pieces.

No procedural noise overlay - the third automatic-fail condition. One noise field composited over the frame would give paper and desk the same grain; they differ in amplitude and in spectral slope: 02_chat paper rms 26.50 slope -1.54 against desk 19.44 / -1.28, 01_pulse paper 19.83 / -0.81 against desk 16.98 / -1.28.

The fold is rendered geometry catching light, not a flat image being transformed - I checked this twice because my first filter was circular. On lossless frames of 06_unfolding.mp4 the flap's shading swings 50.95, 65.28, 57.36 and 40.32 grey levels from its hinge row to its far row across frames 109, 113, 117 and 121 as the plane rotates, and the flap carries texture at rms 4.11 to 5.27 after a 6-px blur against the note face's 2.24 and the desk's 14.76. logs/surfaces.json measures the 142 source frames of unfold_thirds at tooth 1.416 against a floor of 0.6 with none below it.

Tear masks do not repeat on a single screen. Cross-correlating every pair of long edge profiles in 02_chat.png and normalising per overlap rather than per full length, the strongest-looking pair peaks at 0.113 at lag 0; the higher raw figure it first showed came from two pieces my labelling had merged, not from a reused mask. logs/tears.json's count of 5 distinct tears with no repeats holds up.

Feelings are physical objects, not icons. 01_pulse.png at y 1150-1450 x 730-1210 carries a rendered pale dome with radial creases, specular bands and a stem that casts a shadow across its own surface, and a rendered wrapped sweet with twisted foil ends; 07, 08 and 15 add a leaf cluster, a rope loop, a coiled spring and a pinched vessel, all with form and specular rather than flat shapes.

Real, varied scanned stock. 11_chat_scroll.mp4 and 04_moments.png show lined, graph, index, legal and looseleaf pieces with visible tooth and printed rules, and logs/lines.json records the rule pitch running 71.0 to 132.0 px across the ten stills, a ratio of 1.86 against the 1.74 the library's own mm-per-rule figures imply - so different stocks really are different stocks.

Two lighting conditions genuinely exist rather than one graded twice: crops/dusk_pulse.png drops the far-desk mean from 86.6-91.2 in daylight to 71.2-78.3, and its desk falls away from the paper (79.4 to 54.2 going up and out) in a way the daylight stills do not.
verdict: The paper itself is real and I can prove it: no tiling (0.14-0.32 against a synthetic control's 0.840 at its exact period), no shared noise overlay (paper and desk differ in both grain amplitude and spectral slope), stock that varies stock to stock, handwriting with genuine variants (zero of 444 ink components have a twin at IoU 0.99) and genuine pressure (median 49.8 grey levels of core-darkness range within a single glyph), objects that are rendered things rather than icons, and a fold that is real geometry turning under a light - its flap's shading swings 40 to 65 grey levels across the sweep and carries paper tooth. Three things stop it. The blocking one is 04_moments.png, where six voice-note cards are 179,258 pixels of the single literal value #F1ECDF with four of the six containing exactly one colour across their whole area: a beige rectangle standing in for paper, which the row says scores the category below its floor, and which the build's own flat.json flags as ok:false while naming the same construct in its negative control. The second is that nothing in any of the ten stills casts a contact shadow - on the very crop cut to show one, the wood is brighter at the line of contact (105.1) than 127 native pixels away (88.8), and across the whole hero every direction sits within 0.5 grey levels of the bare desk - even though the clips cast a clean directional one, so the row's demand for shadows baked from the render's own lighting is answered by no shadow at all on the artifact it names. The third is that the tears are not tears: the median free edge in nine of ten stills measures under 1.30 px rms and in five of ten sits inside the 0.36-0.59 band torn.json itself records as rejected, while the log's headline pass is measured on the rig's profile generator rather than on the 56 masks the app actually draws. 17 of 25, below the floor of 22, held there by the flat fills in 04_moments.png.
not_worth_opening: evidence/crops/14_media_viewer_strip.png - opened the clip's parent still and the media-viewer crops instead; the strip is six thumbnails of a photograph opening and the photograph is content, not a surface this row judges.

evidence/crops/reception*.png and evidence/logs/reception*.json - the record says in itself that these are a push-reception scene on a different browser and not one of the artifacts; nothing in them is a paper, fold, tear, shadow or ink surface.

evidence/logs/pwa.json, evidence/logs/webpush.txt, evidence/logs/strings.json, evidence/logs/tests.log, evidence/logs/haptics.json, evidence/logs/haptics.check.json - what the page offers an iPhone, the push endpoint, the app's wording, the test run and the vibration patterns. I opened crops/haptics_strip.png and it is a timing chart drawn on a flat field, a diagram rather than a rendered surface, so none of these bear on whether the paper reads as photographed.

evidence/reliability.json, evidence/coldstart.json, evidence/DIFF.json, evidence/logs/scroll_webkit*.json, evidence/logs/11_*.fling.json, evidence/logs/what_the_alternates_cost.json, evidence/logs/*.sound.json, evidence/logs/*.report.json, evidence/logs/manifest.json, evidence/logs/recipes.json - delivery, timing, scroll cost, audio and per-region content records; my row is judged off the pixels and I took every measurement I report myself.

evidence/SCORE.json and evidence/critics/10/messenger_reliability.json - another reader's conclusions. Left closed; I found the second one in the directory I was told to write into and did not open it.

The missing artifacts 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png - I judged the recorded reason rather than the files. It is a reason, not an excuse: WHY_MISSING.json and MANIFEST.json say /dev/kvm is absent so the x86_64 image ran under QEMU instruction emulation, give a measured outcome (adbd answered after 113 minutes, the framework never came up behind it, so no package service to install into), rule out a GTK stand-in, and state that nothing was faked from the PWA. A standing fact about the machine, stated with a measurement, and no substitute passed off as the real thing. The third entry, 15_authored_feeling.mp4 listed as missing because its frame check failed, contradicts frames.json, which marks the same file from_this_run true and checked at the same timestamp; the clip is on disk and I judged it, but the two records disagree about whether it counts.
